Immune

/ih-MYOON/ — stress on MYOON · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is immune to something, such as a disease, is protected from it and will not be affected by it.

After catching chickenpox once, most people are immune for life.

Worked Example

After vaccinating all the patients in the nursing home, the hospital staff ensured they were immune to the flu, protecting the most vulnerable residents.

im (not) + mune (from Latin 'munis,' duty, service) = originally exempt from service. Applied to disease, it means protected from the pathogen's effects — your body is shielded from its harm.

How Immune Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

protected

protected: shielded from harm or infection

resistant

resistant: able to fight off most effects

unsusceptible

unsusceptible: not easily affected or influenced

Antonyms

susceptible

susceptible: easily affected, likely to catch it

vulnerable

vulnerable: open to harm, without defenses

How Strong Is It? — tolerant → hardy → resistant → immune

tolerant vs. immune

tolerant vs. immune: Someone tolerant of cold weather can endure it with some discomfort, but someone immune to a disease is not affected by it at all.

hardy vs. immune

hardy vs. immune: A hardy traveler shrugs off rough conditions, while an immune traveler simply cannot catch the illness no matter the exposure.

resistant vs. immune

resistant vs. immune: A resistant patient fights off most infections; an immune patient is completely protected against this one.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im-

Prefix — im-: not (the form in- takes before b, m, or p) (Latin)

Root — -mune

Root — -mune: duty, service (from Latin munis, 'performing services') (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Im- (not) + Latin munis (duty, service) originally described someone 'exempt from public duty' — excused from what everyone else owed. Over time the meaning narrowed to being exempt from a disease's effects, and figuratively, unaffected by anything at all.

Use the root in a new word: immunize

Use the root in a new word: immunize: The clinic worked all week to immunize every student before flu season began.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Use immune for protection from illness through vaccination or prior exposure — or figuratively, for imperviousness to persuasion or criticism. Caution: the prefix im- (not) doesn't fully explain the meaning; immune signifies 'protected/exempt,' not just a simple negation.
